question.:question/problem:
Consider the augmented matrix $M$ for the variables $x,y,z$ in that order.

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}2 & 6 & 0 & -8 \\ -2 & -6 & 2 & 6 \\ 2 & 8 & -3 & -5\end{array}\right]
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix to row echelon form. Select the resulting augmented matrix.
question.:question/worked-solution:
The augmented matrix is

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}2 & 6 & 0 & -8 \\ -2 & -6 & 2 & 6 \\ 2 & 8 & -3 & -5\end{array}\right]
$$

Normalize the first pivot with $R_1:=\frac{1}{2}R_1$.

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 3 & 0 & -4 \\ -2 & -6 & 2 & 6 \\ 2 & 8 & -3 & -5\end{array}\right]
$$

$R_2:=R_2+(2)R_1$.

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 3 & 0 & -4 \\ 0 & 0 & 2 & -2 \\ 2 & 8 & -3 & -5\end{array}\right]
$$

$R_3:=R_3+(-2)R_1$.

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 3 & 0 & -4 \\ 0 & 0 & 2 & -2 \\ 0 & 2 & -3 & 3\end{array}\right]
$$

The second pivot is zero, while the third row has a nonzero second entry. Exchange $R_2$ and $R_3$.

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 3 & 0 & -4 \\ 0 & 2 & -3 & 3 \\ 0 & 0 & 2 & -2\end{array}\right]
$$

Normalize with $R_2:=\frac{1}{2}R_2$.

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 3 & 0 & -4 \\ 0 & 1 & -\frac{3}{2} & \frac{3}{2} \\ 0 & 0 & 2 & -2\end{array}\right]
$$

Normalize with $R_3:=\frac{1}{2}R_3$.

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 3 & 0 & -4 \\ 0 & 1 & -\frac{3}{2} & \frac{3}{2} \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & -1\end{array}\right]
$$

Thus the row echelon matrix is

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 3 & 0 & -4 \\ 0 & 1 & -\frac{3}{2} & \frac{3}{2} \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & -1\end{array}\right]
$$

question.:question/problem:
Consider the augmented matrix $M$ for the variables $x,y,z$ in that order.

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}2 & -6 & 4 & 4 \\ -1 & 3 & -5 & 3 \\ 1 & -6 & -3 & 3\end{array}\right]
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix to row echelon form, and then solve the linear system. Select the solution $(x,y,z)$.
question.:question/worked-solution:
The augmented matrix is

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}2 & -6 & 4 & 4 \\ -1 & 3 & -5 & 3 \\ 1 & -6 & -3 & 3\end{array}\right]
$$

Normalize the first pivot with $R_1:=\frac{1}{2}R_1$.

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -3 & 2 & 2 \\ -1 & 3 & -5 & 3 \\ 1 & -6 & -3 & 3\end{array}\right]
$$

$R_2:=R_2+(1)R_1$.

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -3 & 2 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & -3 & 5 \\ 1 & -6 & -3 & 3\end{array}\right]
$$

$R_3:=R_3+(-1)R_1$.

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -3 & 2 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & -3 & 5 \\ 0 & -3 & -5 & 1\end{array}\right]
$$

The second pivot is zero, while the third row has a nonzero second entry. Exchange $R_2$ and $R_3$.

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -3 & 2 & 2 \\ 0 & -3 & -5 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & -3 & 5\end{array}\right]
$$

Normalize with $R_2:=-\frac{1}{3}R_2$.

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -3 & 2 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & \frac{5}{3} & -\frac{1}{3} \\ 0 & 0 & -3 & 5\end{array}\right]
$$

Normalize with $R_3:=-\frac{1}{3}R_3$.

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -3 & 2 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & \frac{5}{3} & -\frac{1}{3} \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & -\frac{5}{3}\end{array}\right]
$$

Thus the row echelon matrix is

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -3 & 2 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & \frac{5}{3} & -\frac{1}{3} \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & -\frac{5}{3}\end{array}\right]
$$

Back substitute, starting with the last row:

$$
\begin{aligned}z &=-\frac{5}{3} \\ y &=-\frac{1}{3}-\left(\frac{5}{3}\right)\left(-\frac{5}{3}\right) \\ &=\frac{22}{9} \\ x &=2-(-3)\left(\frac{22}{9}\right) \\ &\quad -(2)\left(-\frac{5}{3}\right) \\ &=\frac{38}{3}\end{aligned}
$$

The solution $(x,y,z)$ is

$$
\left(\frac{38}{3},\frac{22}{9},-\frac{5}{3}\right)
$$

question.:question/problem:
Consider the system of linear equations

\left\{\begin{aligned}3x-3y &=0 \\ -2x+2y-3z &=0 \\ 2x-5y-4z &=-5\end{aligned}\right.
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix to row echelon form, and then solve the linear system. Select the solution $(x,y,z)$.
question.:question/worked-solution:
The augmented matrix is

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}3 & -3 & 0 & 0 \\ -2 & 2 & -3 & 0 \\ 2 & -5 & -4 & -5\end{array}\right]
$$

Normalize the first pivot with $R_1:=\frac{1}{3}R_1$.

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -1 & 0 & 0 \\ -2 & 2 & -3 & 0 \\ 2 & -5 & -4 & -5\end{array}\right]
$$

$R_2:=R_2+(2)R_1$.

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & -3 & 0 \\ 2 & -5 & -4 & -5\end{array}\right]
$$

$R_3:=R_3+(-2)R_1$.

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & -3 & 0 \\ 0 & -3 & -4 & -5\end{array}\right]
$$

The second pivot is zero, while the third row has a nonzero second entry. Exchange $R_2$ and $R_3$.

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & -3 & -4 & -5 \\ 0 & 0 & -3 & 0\end{array}\right]
$$

Normalize with $R_2:=-\frac{1}{3}R_2$.

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & \frac{4}{3} & \frac{5}{3} \\ 0 & 0 & -3 & 0\end{array}\right]
$$

Normalize with $R_3:=-\frac{1}{3}R_3$.

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & \frac{4}{3} & \frac{5}{3} \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 0\end{array}\right]
$$

Thus the row echelon matrix is

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & \frac{4}{3} & \frac{5}{3} \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 0\end{array}\right]
$$

Back substitute, starting with the last row:

$$
\begin{aligned}z &=0 \\ y &=\frac{5}{3}-\left(\frac{4}{3}\right)(0) \\ &=\frac{5}{3} \\ x &=0-(-1)\left(\frac{5}{3}\right) \\ &\quad -(0)(0) \\ &=\frac{5}{3}\end{aligned}
$$

The solution $(x,y,z)$ is

$$
\left(\frac{5}{3},\frac{5}{3},0\right)
$$

$$

question.:question/problem:
Consider the system of linear equations

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}-3x+9y-6z &=-3 \\ -3x+9y-3z &=-5 \\ x-y+2z &=5\end{aligned}\right.
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix to row echelon form, and then solve the linear system. Select the solution $(x,y,z)$.
question.:question/worked-solution:
The augmented matrix is

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}-3 & 9 & -6 & -3 \\ -3 & 9 & -3 & -5 \\ 1 & -1 & 2 & 5\end{array}\right]
$$

Normalize the first pivot with $R_1:=-\frac{1}{3}R_1$.

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -3 & 2 & 1 \\ -3 & 9 & -3 & -5 \\ 1 & -1 & 2 & 5\end{array}\right]
$$

$R_2:=R_2+(3)R_1$.

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -3 & 2 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 3 & -2 \\ 1 & -1 & 2 & 5\end{array}\right]
$$

$R_3:=R_3+(-1)R_1$.

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -3 & 2 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 3 & -2 \\ 0 & 2 & 0 & 4\end{array}\right]
$$

The second pivot is zero, while the third row has a nonzero second entry. Exchange $R_2$ and $R_3$.

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -3 & 2 & 1 \\ 0 & 2 & 0 & 4 \\ 0 & 0 & 3 & -2\end{array}\right]
$$

Normalize with $R_2:=\frac{1}{2}R_2$.

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -3 & 2 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & 3 & -2\end{array}\right]
$$

Normalize with $R_3:=\frac{1}{3}R_3$.

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -3 & 2 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & -\frac{2}{3}\end{array}\right]
$$

Thus the row echelon matrix is

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -3 & 2 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & -\frac{2}{3}\end{array}\right]
$$

Back substitute, starting with the last row:

$$
\begin{aligned}z &=-\frac{2}{3} \\ y &=2-(0)\left(-\frac{2}{3}\right) \\ &=2 \\ x &=1-(-3)(2) \\ &\quad -(2)\left(-\frac{2}{3}\right) \\ &=\frac{25}{3}\end{aligned}
$$

The solution $(x,y,z)$ is

$$
\left(\frac{25}{3},2,-\frac{2}{3}\right)
$$
